title: Radiant expands facilities to support microreactor deployment
html:
The company said it is investing more than USD100 million in the Los Angeles area, adding around 200,000 square feet (about 18,500 square metres) to the manufacturing and R&D footprint at its El Segundo campus which Radiant says will enable it to assemble multiple Kaleidos microreactor units in parallel. The facility supports full research, development and production, incorporating bridge cranes, reactor control-system test containers, in-house turbomachinery and power-generation system production, as well as integrated testing and validation capabilities.

In Tennessee, Radiant is planning to invest USD280 million in its Oak Ridge campus, where construction is already under way, to enable high-rate manufacturing, fuelling and storage. The facility will give it the ability to fuel reactors in a private facility to then be deployed to the customer site in a fuelled, factory-sealed product - Radiant says it will be the only company in the USA able to offer this, which it says will mean it customers will be able to "buy nuclear energy without converting their real estate into a nuclear site through in-ground construction works".

Operations at the fuelling facility are expected to begin in 2027, ahead of planned commercial deliveries in 2028. "By building our fuelling capabilities first and expanding manufacturing in phases, we're putting the infrastructure in place to support initial customer deliveries and scale production as demand increases," the company's Chief Nuclear Officer Rita Baranwal said.

Kaleidos is a transportable high-temperature gas-cooled microreactor generating 3 MW of thermal power or around 1 MW electrical. The whole reactor is designed to fit in a single shipping container: Radiant describes it as a "plug and play" design. Radiant manufactured its first Kaleidos unit in El Segundo - the unit is now at Idaho National Laboratory, where it is undergoing full-scale testing at the Demonstration of Microreactor Experiments (DOME) facility. In late October, the US Department of Energy has granted approval of the reactor's Documented Safety Analysis, a key milestone toward full-power testing. (You can read more about Kaleidos, and other small modular reactor designs, in World Nuclear Association's SMR Design Database.)

Radiant's technology has been selected by the US Army for deployment under the Janus programme with 15 units to be deployed by 2030, the first of which is to be delivered in 2028. The Department of the Air Force has selected Radiant to develop and operate a microreactor at Buckley Space Force Base in Aurora, Colorado while the Department of the Navy has selected the company to support energy independence at Naval Weapons Station Crane in Indiana. In the commercial market, data centre developer and operator Equinix has entered into an agreement with Radiant for 20 units.

"Our El Segundo headquarters strengthens the connection between engineering, innovation and manufacturing, while our Oak Ridge factory establishes the infrastructure to produce and fuel Kaleidos at commercial scale," said Tori Shivanandan, President and COO of Radiant. "Together, these facilities represent a major investment in American nuclear manufacturing and position Radiant to meet growing military and commercial demand and deliver the world's first factory-built, truck-transportable 1 MW commercial nuclear microreactor at scale."
summary: The multimillion-dollar expansion of Radiant's US manufacturing footprint includes a new headquarters and manufacturing facility in California, where its first commercial reactors will be assembled, as well as continued development of its campus in Tennessee.
